Picked this up on the 2.0 branch. The clear button in the Shortcuts filter only renders once you've typed something, and its icon was a lazy import. So the first keystroke was mounting a component that hadn't resolved yet, and that's what kicked focus to the body.

The settings navigation already imports the same icon module up front, so the lazy wrapper wasn't buying anything there. Fixed in #49815, with a regression test that fails on the current code and passes after.

Workaround (Direct SQLite Database Fix):
Users can manually repair their database by updating the stale paths:

Close OpenCode.

Back up the database
```
Copy-Item "$env:USERPROFILE\.local\share\opencode\opencode.db" "$env:USERPROFILE\.local\share\opencode\opencode.db.bak"
```

Run the following SQL updates (using Node.js built-in node:sqlite or any SQLite CLI):
```
-- 1. Update project worktree and name
UPDATE project 
SET worktree = '<NEW_FULL_PATH>',
    name = '<PROJECT_NAME>',
    time_updated = strftime('%s', 'now') * 1000
WHERE id = '<PROJECT_ID>';

-- 2. Update existing sessions pointing to the old path
UPDATE session 
SET directory = REPLACE(directory, '<OLD_PATH>', '<NEW_PATH>'),
    path = REPLACE(path, '<OLD_PATH>', '<NEW_PATH>'),
    time_updated = strftime('%s', 'now') * 1000
WHERE directory LIKE '%<OLD_PATH>%';

-- 3. Update session parts and event logs
UPDATE part SET data = REPLACE(data, '<OLD_PATH>', '<NEW_PATH>') WHERE data LIKE '%<OLD_PATH>%';
UPDATE event SET data = REPLACE(data, '<OLD_PATH>', '<NEW_PATH>') WHERE data LIKE '%<OLD_PATH>%';
```

Restart OpenCode and recreate the project with the right path

Same class of bug, different built-in agent: plan.

Environment: opencode v2.0.8, Linux (official install), Zen free tier (provider Console), no plugins, no other config.

Reproduction (consistent, 100% of attempts, also with --standalone):
1. Add to opencode.json:
"agents": { "plan": { "permissions": [ { "action": "shell", "resource": "*", "effect": "deny" } ] } }
2. opencode run --standalone --agent plan "hi"
3. → Error from provider (Console): OpenCode's free tier can only be used from within OpenCode

Test matrix — same binary, same server, same free-tier models (muse-spark-1.3-contributor-free, big-pickle):

| Agent config | Result |
|---|---|
| plan, no override | ✅ works |
| plan + permissions (even one deny rule) | ❌ gate error |
| plan + description only | ✅ works |
| plan + model only | ✅ works |
| build + permissions override | ✅ works |
| custom agent (any, e.g. reviewer) | ❌ gate error |

Impact: the documented way to lock down the plan agent (agents.plan.permissions) makes that agent unusable on the free tier. Like the explore case, the gate accepts some request paths and rejects others, inside the same CLI.

Workaround for now: drop the agents.plan.permissions override (built-in plan already denies edits outside ~/.opencode/plan and asks before shell commands).

Visual verification complete: **40/40 states identical** across `opencode-light`, `catppuccin-light`, `opencode-dark`, and `dracula-dark` (10 states each). Normalized text and PNGs match. Per-cell comparison found zero visible glyph/background/attribute changes; 116 blank cells differed only in unused foreground metadata.

After tinkering with it a bit more yesterday I found it seemed to be related to the *permissions* of the custom agents, not necessarily the custom agent itself. I haven't yet had the time to go one-by-one and narrow down which specific permission lines are the direct cause, but I did notice that a few of my agents with restrictive permissions (like my `documentation` agent) failed with the same error until I changed the leading permission wildcard from `"*": deny` to `"*": ask` and reloaded the session. 

So it seems one of the permission lines (or perhaps a specific combination of them caught by the wildcard) when set to `deny` is what causes the false-flag. If I end up narrowing it down more I'd be happy to update you with more information. 

Thanks again for your work.

### Deterministic repro on Windows: the gateway rejects `plan` (and any reduced-toolset agent) on the official CLI

Same error as above, on the **official** OpenCode CLI — not a third-party harness.

**Environment:** OpenCode 1.18.31 (latest, no update available), Windows, official Chocolatey/Go binary, logged into OpenCode Go + Zen. Free-tier model `opencode/big-pickle`.

**Repro (two commands, same model, same binary):**

```sh
opencode run --agent build --model opencode/big-pickle "Reply with exactly: PING-OK"
# → PING-OK

opencode run --agent plan --model opencode/big-pickle "Reply with exactly: PING-OK"
# → Error: OpenCode's free tier can only be used from within OpenCode
# log: message=stream ... small=false agent=plan mode=primary → stream error
```

Also reproduced with custom primary agents:
- `planner` (bash/edit/write denied) → fails
- `no-bash` (only `bash` denied, `edit` allowed) → fails
- `build` (full default toolset) → always works

Same model, same session, same binary. The only difference is the `tools` set in the request body — consistent with the gateway's condition `body tools = <opencode builtin tools>`: `plan` (and any agent whose permission profile removes `edit`/`bash`) sends fewer tools than the built-in `build` profile and gets rejected. No `X-Session-ID`/User-Agent issue; those headers are identical.

**Impact:** this is not "other harness" abuse — it's a first-party agent. Any session stored with `agent=plan` cannot be resumed on the free tier; the only workaround is switching the agent to `build` (Tab). `plan` mode is effectively unusable on the free tier from the official CLI. This also affects resume of older sessions, which is how most users are hitting it.

Minor related note: the session-title call (`gpt-5.4-nano`) fails with "Upstream request failed: Insufficient account funds" for the free workspace — non-fatal (title falls back to default).

Could the free-tier check be scoped to `stream=true` + presence of write-capable tools instead of a strict builtin-toolset match, so first-party read-only agents (`plan`) keep working?

I can reproduce this on OpenCode 1.18.31 on Windows, and my case suggests the issue is broader than a single model hitting its own limit.

It looks like OpenCode Go is aggregating the percentage usage of different models into one shared 5-hour / weekly / monthly limit.

For example, my current 5-hour usage is:

- GLM-5.3: $2.5057 / $3.00 = 83.5%
- Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor: $0.8109 / $12.00 = 6.7%
- MiniMax M3: $0.7908 / $12.00 = 6.6%
- GLM-5.3 Flash: $0.56 / $12.00 = 4.7%

Total shown by the dashboard:

83.5 + 6.7 + 6.6 + 4.7 = 101.5%

At this point the 5-hour limit is reached globally.

So in my case, no $60-limit model individually reached anything close to its own 5-hour allowance. Instead, usage percentages from several different models appear to be summed into one global percentage.

The same thing is happening with the monthly limit.

My monthly usage currently shows:

- GLM-5.3: $2.5057 / $15 = 16.7%
- GLM-5.3 Flash: $6.4745 / $60 = 10.8%
- Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor: $3.6967 / $60 = 6.2%
- MiniMax M3: $0.7908 / $60 = 1.3%
- Grok 4.6: $0.02 / $15 = 0.1%

And the dashboard reports:

16.7 + 10.8 + 6.2 + 1.3 + 0.1 = 35.1% monthly usage.

Weekly usage is already 70.2% as well.

This seems inconsistent with the current Go documentation, which says:

> "Each model has the following usage limits: 5-hour — 20% of the monthly limit; weekly — 50%; and monthly — 100%."

That wording strongly suggests per-model limits.

If the intended behavior is actually a single shared normalized quota across all models, then the documentation and model-specific dollar limits are very misleading.

If the intended behavior is truly per-model allowances, then this looks like a quota aggregation bug.

This is particularly problematic when mixing models with different monthly limits. For example, $1 of GLM-5.3 consumes about 6.67 percentage points of the global monthly meter ($15 limit), while $1 of GLM-5.3 Flash consumes only about 1.67 points ($60 limit).

So using even a small amount of an expensive / low-cap model can consume a very large part of the apparent global allowance and then block otherwise mostly-unused models.


Environment:
- OpenCode Desktop 1.18.31
- Windows
- Provider: opencode-go

I'd like to work on this.

I verified both halves against the current tree before commenting:

- `--pure` sets `OPENCODE_PURE=1` in `packages/opencode/src/index.ts`, and the config docs describe it as "skip external plugins entirely", but `packages/core/src/config/plugin/external.ts` scans every `entry.type === "directory"` root for `{plugin,plugins}/*.{ts,js}` without ever consulting `Flag.OPENCODE_PURE` — the file contains no `Flag` reference at all.
- `OPENCODE_DISABLE_PROJECT_CONFIG` is honored by `packages/opencode/src/config/paths.ts` (the older loader, as you noted), while the `.opencode` walk in `packages/core/src/config.ts` is not gated on the flag.

So a project-local plugin file is still imported and executed during startup under either flag, which matches your repro.

Plan: gate the external plugin directory scan on `Flag.OPENCODE_PURE` and the project `.opencode` discovery on `Flag.OPENCODE_DISABLE_PROJECT_CONFIG`, add regression coverage mirroring your repro (a project-local plugin that must not be imported), and run the affected package tests.

One scope question before I start: `packages/core/src/plugin/skill/customize-opencode.md` documents `OPENCODE_PURE=1` as "skip external plugins entirely", while `packages/opencode/specs/tui-plugins.md` says `--pure` / `OPENCODE_PURE` "skips external TUI plugins only". I'll implement the broader documented behavior (no external plugin loaded at startup) unless a maintainer prefers the narrower reading — happy to adjust.
